title: Fix dice bug
body:
## `find_masked_face`/`find_masked_face_2` may share `find_face0`/`find_face`'s zero-fallback bug

**Context**: While diagnosing an age-structure artifact (agents' initial ages silently
defaulting to 0 whenever a random draw exceeded `cumm_age.txt`'s cumulative distribution, which
tops out at 0.9967 instead of 1.0 — see the `find_face0`/`find_face` fix in `mo_agents.f90`,
committed alongside this), two related dice-roll helper functions in the same file were noticed
to have the same-looking pattern:

```fortran
function find_masked_face(r,cum_distr,sides,mask_grav,mask_pop) result(roll)
    ...
    roll = 0
    do j = 1, sides
        if (mask_grav(j) .and. mask_pop(j)) then
            if (r <= cum_distr(j)) then
                roll = j
                exit
            end if
        end if
    end do
end function find_masked_face

(and find_masked_face_2, same structure without the mask_grav check.) Both default roll to
0, an invalid index for their 1-indexed callers — the same failure mode just fixed in the
sibling functions.

Why not fixed together with find_face0/find_far the
gravity-model mobility mechanics, and their fas obvious than the
sibling functions' fix. Because the cumulativeked (only cells passing
mask_grav/mask_pop contribute), the last unmasy sit below 1.0 even
with no upstream bug — so it's not immediately clear whether "default to the last valid face"
(the fix applied to find_face0/find_face) is tor whether a
differently-masked fallback is needed. Needs ier than a copy-paste fix.

Also why it's low urgency right now: mobility (mob=1/ENABLE_MOBILITY) is inactive
(mob=0) in every run this investigation validan't currently exercised
by the Senegal factual/counterfactual runs or the Kenya benchmark.

To do: When mobility work resumes, check whether find_masked_face/find_masked_face_2's
roll=0 fallback is ever actually reachable in practice (i.e. can r exceed the last unmasked
cumulative value under real mask configurations?), and if so, design and apply the correct
fallback semantics for the masked case.
